newsitem.title: USA: Petrobras near completion of record deepwater well.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras near completion of record deepwater well.

text.p: Petrobras is nearing sub-sea completion of its record deepwater Marlim South-3 well, which is expected to be onstream in early June, Exploration and Production Director Antonio Carlos Agostino said on Tuesday.

The Campos well, located in 5,607 feet (1,709 metres) of water and completed with sub-sea and floating production systems, would become the world's deepest producing offshore oil and natural gas well, he said.

That record will stand for about a year, when development of the Brazilian company's newly discovered Roncador field in the northern part of Campos will put a well in 6,561 feet (2,000 metres) of water, he said at the Offshore Technology Conference here.

Petrobras has orders pending on 18 deepwater production units with average capacity of 100,000 barrels of oil per day, including a 180,000 barrel per day unit for Roncador as it moves to expand deepwater exploration and production, he said.
The company also has received 1,000 different proposals for partnering on upstream projects and is in talks on what would be its first-ever domestic joint ventures, partnerships or farm-ins, he said.
